PurposeFounder-level command board for cross-functional exceptions, overrides, temporary deviations, expiry discipline, blocked actions, recovery proof, and return-to-standard controls across live matters.
Source ruleUpdate pricing governance, credit and release control, funding and payables release review, trust posture, claims recovery, CAPA review, founder decisions, matter control, adoption readiness, and linked source records first, then refresh this review.
Founder useKeep temporary exceptions explicit, bounded, reversible, owned, and tied to recovery proof before they become default operating behavior.
Protection ruleThis dashboard governs exception posture only; approved templates, brand assets, and source-record protections stay unchanged.

Exception Control PostureLink

Control lensCurrent postureFounder readRequired response
Exception concentrationMost live exceptions remain clustered around Atlantic Foods.One strategic matter is carrying pricing, release, trust, remedy, and CAPA pressure at once.Consolidate exceptions into a single matter-level map before approvals fragment.
Override disciplineFounder-approved deviations are visible but still need stronger blocked-action language.A narrow yes can be misread as broad permission if the blocked actions are not named.Require each override to state what remains prohibited after approval.
Expiry qualityNo exception is stale, but recovery and return-to-standard logic are uneven.Temporary control is only temporary when the exit is visible.Attach expiry trigger, proof owner, and return-to-standard condition to every live exception.
Founder bandwidthSeveral exceptions still need founder confirmation because controls overlap.Repeated founder calls on the same matter are exception-governance friction.Route repeated founder-rescued exceptions to owner accountability and plan variance.
Normalization riskMedium-high where justified exceptions keep recurring on the same account.The danger is not one exception; it is teaching the system that exceptions are the new rule.Stop expansion until exception count, expiry logic, and recovery evidence improve.

Override Class MatrixLink

Override classWhen it is allowedRequired proofFounder posture
Pricing concession overrideStrategic account capture requires a concession but margin logic and recovery route are visible.Pricing review, profitability view, forecast impact, and founder decision record.Approve narrowly and reprice at the next clean cycle.
Release or credit overrideRelationship timing needs movement but deposit, collection, and exposure guardrails still hold.Credit control, cash forecast, funding release posture, and blocked-action list.Permit only inside documented release boundary.
Trust-fragility overrideStrategic upside is real but counterparty trust posture is not strong enough for normal-speed movement.Trust posture matrix, counterparty response evidence, and return-to-standard trigger.Keep rare, explicit, and time-bound.
Remedy or claims overrideCustomer protection requires temporary tolerance while recovery is pursued.Claims recovery, supplier offset evidence, customer account posture, and margin impact.Approve only with recovery economics and supplier accountability visible.
Preventive-control overrideSupplier or process remains active while CAPA proof is not yet fully verified.CAPA record, supplier performance evidence, verification date, and shipment-risk posture.Hold standard posture until verified prevention closes.

Escalation and Stop RulesLink

RuleConditionRequired escalationFounder action
Expiry breach stopException remains open past review date or proof trigger.Route to founder decision board and active matter control.Freeze expansion until expiry or renewal decision is explicit.
Blanket-permission stopTeam treats a narrow override as permission across payment, release, sourcing, or pricing.Route to control routing, funding release, and trust posture.Restate blocked actions and reverse unauthorized widening.
Recovery missing stopException has no margin, cash, trust, remedy, or prevention recovery path.Route to profitability, claims recovery, CAPA, or capital allocation as relevant.Hold or tighten exception until recovery proof exists.
Founder-rescue repeatSame exception class requires founder call twice in one cycle.Route to owner accountability and plan variance.Treat as owner or system-adoption failure.
Normalization triggerSame exception class repeats across matters or cycles without standard-rule change.Route to control integrity and monthly strategic review.Decide whether to formalize, tighten, or prohibit the pattern.
